key_insight: In benchmark tests, LLMs detected inserted methodological errors in clinical trial reports more often than the earlier experiment’s untrained human reviewers.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest a potential role for LLM-assisted trial review, not evidence of improved cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Tested 15 LLMs, including four open-weight models, on three previously studied randomized trial reports.
Repeated testing on 58 randomized trials published in 2026 to reduce memorization risk.
Used two blinded LLM judges to score 1,796 reviews.
evidence_signal: Major-error detection scores ranged from 53%–96% on the original reports versus a historical human mean of 27%, and from 58%–99% on the 2026 trials.
watch_item: Models also flagged 14%–29% of error types in controls without inserted errors, warranting human verification of flagged concerns.
paper_title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
